title: Type event names and URL patterns
prompt:
Use template literal types to type Cartwheel's strings: - `CheckoutEvent`: `order.` for every `OrderStatus`, plus `payment.` for every `PaymentOutcome`. - `FlagEnvVar`: `CHECKOUT_` followed by each `Feature` in upper case. - `PathParams

`: the names of every `:param` in a route pattern (`never` when there are none). Then implement `buildPath(pattern, params)` at runtime: replace each `:param` with its value from `params`, URL-encoded with `encodeURIComponent`.
hints: `` `order.${OrderStatus}` `` expands to one string per status. `Uppercase<Feature>` works inside a placeholder.
`PathParams` has two cases: a parameter followed by `/` and more path (capture it and recurse on the rest), or a parameter at the very end.
At runtime, `pattern.replace(/:(\w+)/g, (_, name) => …)` visits each parameter name. Treat `params` as `Record<string, string | number>` inside with one commented cast.
explanation: A union inside a template literal expands into one string per member, so both event families are derived from the existing unions. `Uppercase` transforms each feature name. `PathParams` pattern-matches the route: `infer Param` captures the text after a colon up to the next `/`, and the recursive call handles the rest of the path; the final branch catches a parameter at the end. `Record, …>` then makes every parameter a required key of `params`, so a missing `lineId` is a compile error rather than a request to `/orders/1042/lines/undefined`.

checks.types: The file type-checks with zero errors, including all type tests
checks.builds: `buildPath` fills in every parameter and leaves parameter-free paths alone
